title: A Look at Adventure Tactics with a focus on the Character Level Up System
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B_OF2TYLnQw

Daniel (@dungeondive) takes a look at Adventure Tactics: Domianne Tower, a game he'd never heard of until Jerry Hawthorne mentioned it on the Dungeon Dive Facebook group — and he's learned that when Jerry names a game, it's worth a closer look.

The shorthand he offers is "my first Gloomhaven": a deckbuilding co-op skirmish game run through a spiral-bound campaign. But the comparison stops quickly, because he thinks he likes this one more. The star is the levelling system, which he calls a new standard for character advancement in fantasy adventure games. You start from one of five D&D archetypes, then every level offers genuinely exciting choices — new cards for your deck, passive abilities you select three of per scenario, multiclass paths — and it's the thing that pulls you through the campaign.

The campaign itself branches: skull symbols mark the harder path, bonus objectives feed perks and encrypted notes forward into later choices, and each scenario's rules sit on a single page. He loves the standees, mocks the handful of absurdly undersized hero miniatures, and flags the genuinely warped cardboard as a known printing fault. His other gripe is dull, non-interactive battle maps. Still: highly recommended, and a strong family pick.

----

Adventure Tactics puts its best ideas in the level-up deck rather than the battle map — would you rather a game invest in how your character grows or in the terrain they fight across?
